clue.text: Prisoner's label tucked into socks

indicators.note: something tucked into a garment sits inside it, so 'label' goes inside 'socks'

blocks.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks
a tag is a label, as on luggage or clothing

explanation.surface: A convict's name tag stuffed inside a pair of socks.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but is really 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held captive as security for a demand is a kind of captive or detainee, hence a prisoner.

clue.text: Maybe Bob Harris's debut transformed radio?

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so we keep only the opening letter of 'Harris'
whatever is transformed changes its form, so the letters of 'radio' are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of Harris
anagram fodder, five letters

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the broadcaster Bob Harris's first show changed radio for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Harris is a veteran BBC radio DJ, so 'Bob' looks like a first name; it is the haircut, and 'Maybe' flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is one particular short haircut style, so it is an example of a styled head of hair.

clue.text: Threadbare throw worn by abbess

indicators.note: a garment worn by someone wraps around them, so 'throw' goes around 'abbess'

blocks.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy
abbess cut to its first three letters, the dictionary abbreviation Abb.

explanation.surface: A nun in charge wearing a worn-out shawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' looks like a blanket or shawl, which suits the picture; it is the verb, as at a fairground coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth that is worn thin through long use looks scruffy and shabby; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Skilfully coats item in liquid with 100% effectiveness

indicators.note: a layer that coats something surrounds it, so 'Skilfully' wraps 'item in liquid'

blocks.note: ably means with skill
a solute is the substance dissolved in a liquid solvent

explanation.surface: A chemistry demonstration: something expertly coated so it works perfectly in a fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item in liquid' is a chemistry definition for the dissolved substance, not a physical object floating there.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something totally, completely and without any reservation is the same as doing it fully or entirely.

clue.text: John almost upended George

indicators.note: almost all of something means stopping just short, so the last letter of 'John' is dropped
turning something upside down in a down clue runs it bottom to top, reversing the letters

blocks.note: john is American slang for a lavatory, TOILET, with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: Two Beatles, John and George, one nearly toppling the other.
explanation.walkthrough: John and George look like Beatles; John is really a toilet and George is the Victorian novelist George Eliot, author of Middlemarch.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot was the pen name of Mary Ann Evans, the novelist, so the first name leads to the surname.

clue.text: One sometimes working to restore mobile bars?

definitions.text: One sometimes working to restore mobile bars?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who repairs pubs or snack counters on wheels
setter's reading: the signal or battery bars on a mobile phone screen, filled up again by a plug-in device

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile bars' suggests travelling pubs; on a phone the bars are the battery level, and 'sometimes working' is a nod to how temperamental such cables are.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug-in device that refills a phone battery is exactly what this word names in everyday use.

clue.text: California holiday? Look up somewhere to eat

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means reading from bottom to top, so 'Look' runs backwards

blocks.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
a fête is a festival or holiday
an air is a look or manner, as in 'an air of confidence'

explanation.surface: Planning a Californian holiday and looking up places to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up' reads as a single phrasal verb, research; split it, and 'Look' is a noun for an appearance while 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service restaurant, typically in a workplace or school, is a place where people go for meals.

clue.text: A measure of port

blocks.note: a unit of land area
an ancient harbour city on the coast of northern Israel

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a drinks order, a measure of the fortified wine; split it after 'measure', and port is a harbour town, Acre in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, and Acre is also the name of a historic Mediterranean harbour city.

clue.text: Security measure upset travel beyond Driffield following evacuation, by gum!

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so 'travel' reads from the bottom up
evacuating a word empties out its middle, so only the outer letters of 'Driffield' stay
one thing beyond another comes after it, so 'travel' is placed after 'Driffield'

blocks.note: guar gum is a thickener made from guar beans
Driffield with all its inside letters removed
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire traveller upset about a security precaution, exclaiming 'By gum!' in local fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum!' is a mild Northern English exclamation and Driffield is a Yorkshire market town; here 'by' just means next to, placing the gum first.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog kept to protect a property from intruders is one way of keeping it safe, a protective measure.

clue.text: Perhaps Queen fan is inspired by improvisation of Taylor

indicators.note: an improvisation makes something up on the spot, so the letters of 'Taylor' are freely rearranged
to be inspired is to be breathed in, so 'is' is taken inside the other letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, six letters
used as it stands

explanation.surface: A fan of the band Queen thrilled by drummer Roger Taylor's improvised playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger Taylor is Queen's drummer, so the rock band reading is strong; the queen meant is a monarch, and 'Perhaps' marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the monarchy, such as an admirer of the reigning sovereign, is called by this word.

clue.text: Is surrounding old lady with religious leaders

indicators.note: 'Is' is split to go all round 'old lady', which sits in the middle

blocks.note: used as it stands
one's old lady is informally one's mother, a mam

explanation.surface: An elderly woman encircled by clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old lady' is slang for mother, and mam is the Northern and Welsh form.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the men who lead prayers in a mosque, and so are Islamic religious figures.

clue.text: Trendy set fairly regularly coming to place for treatments

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from 'fairly' keeps every second one

blocks.note: in means fashionable
set means firm, as a jelly sets
the second, fourth and sixth letters of fairly

explanation.surface: A fashionable crowd drifting fairly often to a spa for beauty treatments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trendy set' reads as one noun phrase, a fashionable crowd; it is two separate pieces, an adjective and then a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital, or a sick bay in a school or institution, is where patients receive medical care.

clue.text: Make weak argument defending current literature

indicators.note: to defend something is to put a guard around it, so 'argument' surrounds the rest

blocks.note: a debate is a formal argument
I is the symbol for electric current
lit is the common short form of literature

explanation.surface: A feeble case made in support of contemporary books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make weak argument' reads as a verb phrase about arguing badly; the definition stops after 'Make weak'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap someone's strength or enfeeble them is to reduce their vigour, the plain meaning here.

clue.text: Object of love left after part of wedding service?

indicators.note: 'left' is placed after the wedding words, so it comes at the end

blocks.note: the vow 'I do' spoken at a wedding
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A jilted lover left alone after the vows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like jilted or abandoned; it is simply the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adored or worshipped, such as a pop star or film hero, is the target of devotion.

clue.text: Mushy peas and rice stored in iron apparatus for emergency use

indicators.note: mushy food has lost its shape, so 'peas and rice' are mashed into a new order
goods stored in a container sit inside it, so the mashed letters go inside 'iron'

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
anagram fodder, eight letters; 'and' just joins them

explanation.surface: Emergency rations of mushy peas and rice kept in an iron pot.
explanation.walkthrough: Mushy peas are a British side dish of mashed marrowfat peas, which makes the food picture convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: An external staircase or ladder lets people leave a burning building, so it is equipment kept for such crises.

clue.text: TV show that rioters condemned

indicators.note: a condemned building is wrecked, so 'that rioters' is knocked into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eleven letters

explanation.surface: A television programme that rioters have denounced.
explanation.walkthrough: The Traitors is a hit BBC reality game show in which players try to unmask hidden traitors; the surface fits, since traitors too are condemned.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a reality television programme, a popular BBC game series, so the whole title is one broadcast.

clue.text: Discovered one of crew coming round queasy - quiet below deck!

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its cover taken off, so 'one of crew' loses its outer letters
to come round is to turn about, so 'queasy' runs backwards
in a down clue what sits below comes after, so 'quiet' goes above the definition, at the end

blocks.note: a member of a crew, with its first and last letters stripped away
feeling ill, sick
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A sailor found coming round seasick, told to be quiet below decks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below deck' reads as a nautical phrase, which is the misdirection; 'deck' is the definition, a verb meaning adorn, and 'Discovered' means stripped of its covering.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something, as in decking the halls, is to adorn or decorate it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Parisian curls first tee shot

indicators.note: something shot is broken or ruined, so 'first tee' is scattered into new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: A golfer in Paris whose opening drive curls off the tee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First tee shot' is golfing language, and 'curls' reads as the ball swerving; the definition is the hairstyle, French in origin.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, borrowed from French, names a fringe of small curled locks worn across the forehead.

clue.text: Grazing rat gets hold of rubbish

indicators.note: to get hold of something is to grip it, so 'rat' wraps around 'rubbish'

blocks.note: to rat on someone is to inform, or sing to the police
crap is slang for rubbish

explanation.surface: A rat feeding on a heap of refuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grazing' looks like feeding and 'rat' like the animal, which suits the scavenging picture; both are verbs of another sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Grazing the skin means rubbing it roughly against a surface, abrading it, which is what this word also describes.

clue.text: Flustered caterer missing last pound stops to double-check the scales

indicators.note: 'caterer' missing its last letter loses the final one of its seven
someone flustered is thrown into confusion, so the shortened 'caterer' is jumbled
a stopper plugs the middle of something, so 'pound' is placed inside the jumble

blocks.note: caterer without its final letter
libra is the Roman pound, source of the abbreviation lb

explanation.surface: A flustered cook, a pound short, halts to recheck the kitchen weighing scales.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman libra gives the lb abbreviation and is also the zodiac sign of the scales, which ties it neatly to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset a measuring instrument so its readings are accurate again is to check and adjust it once more.

clue.text: After first day off insensitive student body withdraws ice cream

indicators.note: taking away the first 'day' abbreviation from 'insensitive' removes its opening letter
to withdraw is to draw back, so the whole string runs backwards

blocks.note: insensitive is DEAD, as a numb limb, and the first D (day) is removed
the NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: After a day off, a thick-skinned student union pulls its ice cream from sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is the UK's National Union of Students; 'withdraws' looks like pulling something from sale but reverses everything before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert of scoops topped with syrup, nuts or fruit is a classic served dish of frozen dairy.

clue.text: Essentially, Canadian shivered into the period before Christmas

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the middle two letters are taken from each of the next three words

blocks.note: the central pair of letters of Canadian
the central pair of letters of shivered
the central pair of letters of into

explanation.surface: A Canadian shivering through the cold weeks leading up to Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a link word but it is fodder too; all three words give their middle pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The church season of four weeks leading up to the Nativity feast is the time of preparation.

clue.text: Take a picture as camera tracks along from right to left

indicators.note: reading from right to left runs an across entry backwards, so 'camera tracks along' is read in reverse

blocks.note: a camera pans when it swings horizontally to follow a subject

explanation.surface: A photographer shooting as the camera sweeps sideways across a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue sounds like film-making, and the reversal indicator reads as the camera's direction of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a quick photograph is informally described with this verb, as in a holiday photo.

clue.text: Extremely safe scan

blocks.note: ultra means extremely, as in ultra-modern
sound means safe and secure, as in safe and sound

explanation.surface: Reassurance that a medical scan carries no risk at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads naturally, since this kind of scan is famously harmless; the adjectives split cleanly into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical imaging using high-frequency waves, used for example during pregnancy, is a common type of examination.

clue.text: Correct change of direction in Sun?

blocks.note: correct means accurate, true
a turn is a change of direction, and the Sun newspaper leans to one political side

explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper with a conservative political slant; its direction is the political wing, and a turn that way is a change of direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate and true is one sense; the other is the side of the political spectrum, a conservative leaning, or a turn.

clue.text: Climbing, sex or bread?

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue goes from bottom to top, so 'sex or' reads upwards

blocks.note: it is a coy word for sex
used as it stands

explanation.surface: A choice between rock climbing, sex or a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a link offering alternatives; it is part of the fodder, reading upwards with 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an unleavened flatbread from South Asia, cooked on a griddle and eaten with curries.

clue.text: Trimming rear seal

blocks.note: the tail is the rear end
an O-ring is a rubber loop used as a seal

explanation.surface: Clipping the back end of a seal, perhaps at a zoo grooming session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' looks like the animal and 'rear' like its hindquarters; it is an engineering part, the ring-shaped gasket.
explanation.definitionFit: Adapting and cutting cloth to fit, or adjusting anything to suit, involves cutting down and shaping, hence trimming.

clue.text: Become confused retracting upheld damage claims

indicators.note: the phrase 'upheld damage' lays claim to the letters, holding them inside it
retracting draws something back, so the held letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: letters running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An insurer getting muddled as it withdraws damage claims it had previously accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damage claims' reads as an insurance phrase, but 'claims' is the indicator and the letters straddle 'upheld' and 'damage'.
explanation.definitionFit: When the mind becomes muddled or befuddled, this verb describes that state, like an egg going off.

clue.text: Exploited shingle originally from Brighton?

indicators.note: something exploited is worked over and used up, so the letters of 'shingle' are worked into new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, seven letters

explanation.surface: Pebbles taken from the beach at Brighton, a seaside town on England's south coast famous for its stony shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks like a first-letters indicator; it belongs to the definition, someone born in Brighton, and the question mark flags that this is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone born in Brighton is by birth a native of England, so their nationality is given by this adjective.

clue.text: Get her eating nibbles on that account

indicators.note: a nibble takes a small bite out of something, so the answer is a small bite of 'Get her eating'

blocks.note: letters running across all three words

explanation.surface: Urging someone to get her snacking on a few nibbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nibbles' looks like party snacks; it is the verb, taking a bite out of the phrase before it.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic adverb means for that reason or because of that, so it is an old synonym.
